nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $F$ a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, and $v \in R^\sigma$. The constant term of the Taylor expansion $F(X + v)$, obtained by substituting $X_i + v_i$ for each $X_i$, is the value $F(v)$.
nodes.title: Constant term of the Taylor expansion

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a module over a division ring $K$. For every nonzero scalar $a \in K$ and every nonzero vector $v \in V$, the points of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(V)$ represented by $a v$ and by $v$ are equal.
nodes.title: Rescaling a representative does not change the projective point

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. For every $a \in K$, the constant polynomial $a$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ has multiplicity $0$ at every point $p$ of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$. For $a = 0$ this is the junk value of the multiplicity of the zero polynomial.
nodes.title: Constants have multiplicity zero

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a homogeneous polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every nonzero $v \in K^\sigma$, the multiplicity of $F$ at the point $[v]$ of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ spanned by $v$ equals the order of vanishing of $F$ at $v$, with the value $\infty$ read as $0$.
nodes.title: The multiplicity can be computed at any representative

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $F \neq 0$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, and $p$ a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ with chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$. The multiplicity of $F$ at $p$ is positive if and only if $F(\bar p) = 0$.
nodes.title: Positive multiplicity means vanishing

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ a finite type and $w \in K^\sigma$ nonzero, and let $p$ be a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ that is not orthogonal to the point $[w]$ spanned by $w$, that is, $p$ does not lie on the hyperplane $\sum_i w_i x_i = 0$. Then the linear form $\sum_i w_i X_i$ has multiplicity $0$ at $p$.
nodes.title: A hyperplane has multiplicity zero off it

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ a finite type and $w \in K^\sigma$ nonzero, and let $p$ be a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ orthogonal to the point $[w]$ spanned by $w$, that is, $p$ lies on the hyperplane $\sum_i w_i x_i = 0$. Then the linear form $\sum_i w_i X_i$ has multiplicity $1$ at $p$.
nodes.title: A hyperplane has multiplicity one at its points

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. The multiplicity of $F$ at a point $p$ of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ is the order of vanishing of $F$ at the chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$ of $p$, as a natural number, with the value $\infty$ read as $0$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a polynomial at a projective point

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be an integral domain of characteristic zero, $F$ a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, $v \in R^\sigma$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $F$ vanishes to order at least $n + 1$ at $v$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$ and every first partial derivative $\partial F / \partial X_i$ vanishes to order at least $n$ at $v$.
nodes.title: Order of vanishing via first partial derivatives

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F \neq 0$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every point $p$ of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$, the multiplicity of $F$ at $p$, viewed in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, equals the order of vanishing of $F$ at the chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$ of $p$.
nodes.title: The multiplicity of a nonzero polynomial is its order of vanishing

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F$ of $F$ at $v$ is at least $1$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$.
nodes.title: Vanishing to order at least one

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and let $a \in R$ be nonzero. For every point $v \in R^\sigma$, the constant polynomial $a$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v a = 0$ at $v$.
nodes.title: Nonzero constants vanish to order zero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of $F$ at $v$ equals $\infty$ if and only if $F = 0$.
nodes.title: Only the zero polynomial vanishes to infinite order

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F$ of $F$ at $v$ is $0$ if and only if $F(v) \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Vanishing to order zero

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $F$ be a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ that is homogeneous of some degree $d$. For every nonzero $c \in K$ and every point $v \in K^\sigma$, the orders of vanishing agree: $\operatorname{ord}_{cv} F = \operatorname{ord}_v F$.
nodes.title: Scaling invariance of the order of vanishing

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\sigma$ be a finite set and let $w, v \in K^\sigma$ with $w \neq 0$ and $w \cdot v = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i v_i = 0$. Then the linear form $L = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i X_i$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v L = 1$ at $v$.
nodes.title: A nonzero linear form vanishes to order one on its hyperplane

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\sigma$ be a finite set and let $w, v \in K^\sigma$ with $w \cdot v = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i v_i \neq 0$. Then the linear form $L = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i X_i$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v L = 0$ at $v$.
nodes.title: A linear form vanishes to order zero off its hyperplane

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. The order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of $F$ at $v$ is the order at the origin of the Taylor expansion $F(v + X)$, the polynomial obtained from $F$ by substituting $X_i + v_i$ for each $X_i$: the least total degree of a monomial with nonzero…
nodes.title: Order of vanishing at a point

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $m$ a finite set. Let $p, q$ be points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^m)$ and let $\hat p, \hat q \in K^m$ be the fixed nonzero representatives chosen for $p$ and $q$. Then $p$ and $q$ are orthogonal (the dot product of a representative of $p$ with a representative of $q$ vanishes, which does not depend on the representatives) if and only if $\hat p \cdot \hat q = 0$.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of projective points via representatives

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_j)_{j \in \sigma}$, let $v \in R^\sigma$ and let $i \in \sigma$. Writing $G(X + v)$ for the polynomial obtained from a polynomial $G$ by substituting $X_j + v_j$ for each $X_j$, we have $\frac{\partial}{\partial X_i}\bigl(F(X + v)\bigr) = \frac{\partial F}{\partial X_i}(X + v)$.
nodes.title: Partial derivatives commute with Taylor expansion

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be an integral domain of characteristic zero and let $F$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every point $v \in R^\sigma$, the polynomial $F$ vanishes to order at least $2$ at $v$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$ and $\frac{\partial F}{\partial X_i}(v) = 0$ for every $i \in \sigma$.
nodes.title: Vanishing to order at least two via first partial derivatives

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
